chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadah, from 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent a man from his companions as a governor and said to him: 'I have sent you to the people of Allah, meaning the people of Mecca, so forbid them from the sale of what has not been taken possession of, and from two conditions in one sale, and from profit on what is not guaranteed.'

key_terms.بَيْعُ مَا لَمْ يُقْبَضْ: Sale of goods before taking possession
key_terms.رِبْحُ مَا لَمْ يُضْمَنْ: Profit on what is not guaranteed

ai.seo_question: What are the three main prohibitions in Islamic trade law mentioned in this hadith from Sahih al-Tahdhib?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Prophet’s direct instruction to a governor in Mecca, establishing foundational prohibitions in Islamic commercial law: avoiding the sale of undelivered goods, preventing the combination of two contracts in one, and ensuring profit is tied to actual risk. These rulings underscore the Shia scholarly emphasis on transparency and fairness in trade, reflecting the practical application of prophetic guidance to maintain economic justice in early Muslim communities.
